paper_title: In Situ Measurements of Dark Photon Dark Matter Using Parker Solar Probe: Going beyond the Radio Window
suggested_experiment_name: Parker Solar Probe (PSP) in-situ DPDM search
coupling_convention: epsilon * (rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5 — kinetic mixing parameter scaled by square root of local DPDM density fraction, as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 2
notes: Paper presents new 95% C.L. observed limits on dark photon kinetic mixing epsilon using in-situ Parker Solar Probe (and STEREO) radio spectrometer data, via resonant DPDM-to-photon conversion in solar wind plasma. Valid mass range m_A' ~ 3e-10 to 8e-8 eV (70 kHz - 20 MHz), with epsilon <~ 1e-14 - 1e-13. No numerical table is provided; the emitted data_points are an approximate reconstruction of the Fig. 2 envelope based on the stated range (endpoints ~1e-13, best sensitivity ~1e-14 at intermediate masses), hence the moderate extraction confidence. Limits quoted as epsilon*(rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5, i.e. assuming DPDM constitutes the full local DM density (standard ~0.3 GeV/cm^3, not explicitly restated in excerpt).
